headline: Trilateral talks could be held in early November following Witkoff–Putin meeting, Zelensky says
standfirst: Ukraine, the United States and Russia will hold discussions to work out the agenda for a trilateral meeting that could take place in early November, although the exact date has yet to be set.
body_markdown:
Ukraine, the United States and Russia will hold discussions to work out the agenda for a trilateral meeting that could take place in early November, although the exact date has yet to be set. (Ukrinform)

**Axios** adds: Russian President Vladimir Putin told White House envoy Steve Witkoff on Wednesday that he "agrees in principle" resuming trilateral peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. to end the war, the Kremlin said. Why it matters: The White House hopes Putin will show more willingness to compromise after President Trump agreed to lift sanctions on Russian diesel sales and took other steps welcomed by Moscow.

**South China Morning Post** adds: Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month, the Kremlin said on Wednesday, after Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in Washington’s latest push to stop Europe’s bloodiest conflict since second world war.
